content: The Monumental Heritage of Lanna Located in the heart of Chiang Mai’s Old City, Wat Chedi Luang is home to the largest pagoda (Chedi) in the province. Originally built in the 14th century, it once stood 80 meters tall before being partially destroyed by an earthquake in 1545. Despite its ruined state, the massive brick structure—adorned with iconic stone elephants—remains a powerful symbol of Lanna craftsmanship and resilience. The temple complex also houses the "Sao Inthakin" (City Pillar), the sacred guardian of Chiang Mai.
title: Wat Chedi Luang
